results.title: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator protects neurons after ...
results.content: Neurons were divided into the control, control + rtPA, hemin (to induce ICH _in vitro_), and hemin + rtPA groups (rtPA treatment concurrently with hemin) (_n_ = 3/group) and analyzed by RNA sequencing analysis, western blot assay, electron microscopy, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-tracker, and immunofluorescence staining at 24 hours after drug treatment. ### Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator inhibits neuron apoptosis, excessive autophagy, and endoplasmic reticulum stress by upregulating PI3K/AKT/mTOR in the _in vitro_ intracerebral hemorrhage cell model. AKT: RAC-alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase; DEGs: differential expression genes; DMSO: dimethyl sulfoxide; ICH: intracerebral hemorrhage; KEGG: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes; LC3: microtubule-associated proteins 1A/1B light chain 3B; LY294002: PI3K inhibitor; mTOR: mammalian target of rapamycin; p62: sequestosome-1/ubiquitin-binding protein p62; PI3K: phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase regulatory subunit alpha; rtPA: recombinant tissue plasminogen activator. These results suggest that the protective effects of rtPA reduce apoptosis, inhibit excessive autophagy, and modulate ER stress in the ICH cell model _in vitro_ through the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
